papers.title: Quantum-Information Probes of Collapse Dynamics in Causal Fermion Systems
papers.abstract: Finster, Kleiner, and Paganini derived from causal fermion systems (CFS) a nonrelativistic effective collapse model whose statistical operator obeys, to leading order, a Kossakowski--Lindblad equation. In the factorized regime of that derivation, the dissipator is built from purely spatial operators $N_{k,a}$ with positive rates fixed by microscopic time-nonlocal kernels. We translate this CFS-specific generator into quantities accessible to coherent quantum processors. The resulting CFS Dirichlet form obeys an exact purity-loss identity under arbitrary Hamiltonian control, and its null algebra is the commutant of the $*$-algebra generated by the projected $N_{k,a}$. For joint eigenbranches we obtain an exact distinguishability functional controlling exponential coherence loss and a lower bound on channel distance from ideal unitary evolution. In an $n$-qubit dephasing sector, the projected kernels generate a positive-semidefinite covariance matrix $C$, with GHZ visibility $\exp[-2T\bm{1}^{\mathsf T}C\bm{1}]$. We prove that uniformly summable finite-range correlations yield at most $O(n)$ GHZ decay, whereas $O(n^2)$ scaling requires a collective non-summable component. Single- and two-qubit cat coherences reconstruct $C$, giving a covariance-spectroscopy protocol, while Knill--Laflamme conditions characterize first-order correctability of the projected CFS error algebra. We also derive an explicit compatibility inequality between macroscopic state reduction and long coherent computation and show why absence of probe heating does not imply absence of coherence signatures. The results do not exclude CFS: its covariance strength, $\ellmin$, and hardware projection remain underdetermined. They instead identify the microscopic input required for a genuine no-go theorem and establish scalable quantum processors as direct probes of the CFS collapse sector.

papers.title: A boundary limit for Suzuki's arithmetic canonical system
papers.abstract: For the shifted Riemann xi-function, we prove the large-radius boundary limit of Suzuki's arithmetic canonical system. The proof applies to every positive shift for which the reflected quotient is pole-free in the upper half-plane and the two entire functions have no common zero. It therefore applies unconditionally to shifts at least one half, including Suzuki's original range greater than one. We give the weak-kernel construction needed at the smaller shifts, two integral identities for its positive determinant ratio, and decay estimates faster than every fixed exponential in logarithmic radius. The hypotheses on the shift are retained throughout.

papers.title: A proof that $\mathbb{Z}$ is Diophantine in $\mathbb{Q}$ through congruent-number twists
papers.abstract: We give a proof of Glazer and collaborators' theorem that $\mathbb{Z}$ is Diophantine in $\mathbb{Q}$, which builds on OpenAI's proof that Hilbert's tenth problem over $\mathbb{Q}$ has a negative answer. Integers are represented by multiples of a point on an elliptic curve of rank one over $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt2)$. An existential condition on two congruent-number twists forbids poles of odd order at odd primes. A height bound at six rational points, from a quaternionic Shimura curve and Serre's conjecture (a theorem of Khare–Wintenberger and Kisin), and a prime pattern from the Green–Tao–Ziegler theorem turn congruences at chosen primes into identities between multiples, and the growth of a Lucas sequence forces integrality. Our contribution is the existence of the rational points that the condition on twists requires: for coprime squarefree integers $\beta>1$ and $\theta\ge1$ with $\beta\equiv\theta\equiv1\pmod8$, each a square modulo the primes of the other, there is an integer $e$ such that $y^2=x^3-e^2x$ and $y^2=x^3-e^2\theta^2x$ both have rank one and a rational point with abscissa in $\beta\mathbb{Q}^{\times2}$. Where Glazer and collaborators use a restricted $2$-converse theorem, this rests on published theorems: the genus criterion of Tian, Yuan and Zhang, with Gross–Zagier.

papers.title: A superlogarithmic lower bound for deterministic word separation
papers.abstract: Let $S(n)$ be the maximum, over distinct binary words of length $n$, of the least number of states in a complete deterministic finite automaton that accepts exactly one of them. We prove $S(n)\geq(1-o(1))\log n\log\log n$. The main step is a common word of length $\exp(O(\sqrt{k}\log k))$ that, after suitable powering of the generators, reaches the sink components of every transformation pair on $k$ states and attains minimum rank on each sink. This transfers the balanced positive permutation identities of Xu and Regan to the full transformation monoid without changing their leading logarithmic length. The conclusion concerns deterministic automata; it makes no assertion about nondeterministic separators.

papers.title: An effective André–Oort theorem for Shimura varieties
papers.abstract: We give effective bounds for the special subvarieties $V$ that are maximal in a subvariety $Z$ of a Shimura variety, in terms of the degree of $Z$: for the degree of $V$, with no hypothesis; and for the discriminant of a number field $L_V$ attached to $V$ and the Klingler–Yafaev invariant $\alpha_V$ of the level, if for some $\delta>0$ the Dedekind zeta function of $L_V$ has no zero with real part greater than $1-\delta$. Here $Z$ is geometrically irreducible and defined over a number field, the level is neat and of product form, and the bounds are explicit in the degree of $Z$ and, for $L_V$ and $\alpha_V$, also in the degree of the field and $\delta$, with constants that are effectively computable from the Shimura datum, the level and representatives of the connected components of the adjoint Shimura variety. A preprint of Cureton and Thorner, whose proof has been formalized in Lean, establishes such a half-plane with $\delta=1/32$ for every number field; granting it, all these bounds hold with no further hypothesis. For abelian type, an algorithm lists these subvarieties from the bounds, given a finite étale cover by a Shimura variety of Hodge type inside one of Mumford's moduli spaces and equations for the preimage of $Z$.

papers.title: An Elementary Proof of Fundamental Theorem of Algebra over Rationals
papers.abstract: We, with the aid of AI, give an elementary proof of the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra over Rationals, i.e., for any nonconstant polynomial $f$ with rational complex number coefficients and every positive rational number $\eps$, there exists a rational complex number $z$ such that $Q(f(z))<\eps^2$. The proof is constructive and relies only on finite rational arithmetic, without using real numbers, infinite sets, or related concepts.

papers.title: An ergodic classification of smooth type subshifts over odd two-letter alphabets
papers.abstract: Fix distinct positive odd integers $\alpha<\beta$. We classify the invariant probability measures of the smooth subshifts obtained by prescribing the successive run types. Every such subshift is uniquely ergodic if $\alpha\ge3$ or $\{\alpha,\beta\}=\{1,3\},\{1,5\}$. For $\alpha=1$ and $\beta\ge7$, unique ergodicity holds exactly for directives containing infinitely many zeros; every other directive gives precisely two ergodic measures. The proof combines a two-dimensional frequency recursion with recognized run decompositions and explicit control of the density of decomposition boundaries.

papers.title: An Explicit Lower Bound for the Proportion of Isolated Zeros of the Riemann Zeta Function
papers.abstract: We study isolation in the full sequence of nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function with positive ordinate, counted with multiplicity. For every fixed $0<c\le10^{-5}$, we prove unconditionally that the lower limiting proportion of zeros whose two neighboring gaps both exceed $2\pi c/\log X$ is at least $0.672468$. Here $X$ is the common height cutoff and the neighbors are taken from the infinite sequence. This refines Lamzouri's small-fixed-gap bound $0.6552\ldots$. We retain his isolation argument and the Montgomery–Taylor kernel, while replacing the linear cost of horizontal displacement by a certified majorant with a positive threshold. Young's shifted mollified second moment bounds the corresponding truncated displacement moment. We supply the boundary and global-height arguments and obtain a gap loss $6\pi^2c^2$ uniform under the required smoothing. A fixed interval-arithmetic certificate completes the numerical estimate. The result is asymptotic and gives no effective first height.

papers.title: An Unconditional Artin-Matthews Theorem For Simultaneous Primitive Roots
papers.abstract: Let S be a finite set of integers diﬀerent from 0 and ±1. We prove that the primes for which every member of S is a primitive root have positive lower relative density precisely when neither of Matthews’ two obstructions occurs. The proof uses the marked estimates for prime predecessors and uniform splitting estimates of OpenAI. Its principal step is a refinement of the large-prime-factor law for prime predecessors by a fixed cubic Frobenius condition. We obtain this refinement from a shifted bilinear estimate for cubic theta series, a divisor-weighted positive sieve estimate, and a prime-extraction argument that retains the natural Hecke coeﬃcients. The resulting lower bound holds in every suﬃciently large dyadic interval.

papers.title: At least one of β(4), β(6), …, β(32) is irrational
papers.abstract: For the Dirichlet beta function, we prove that at least one of $\beta(4),\beta(6),\ldots,\beta(32)$ is irrational. This reduces Krisman's seventeen-value set $\beta(4),\beta(6),\ldots,\beta(36)$ (Hexagon 2610.00285v2) to fifteen values. The improvement comes from a sharper denominator estimate for his construction.

papers.title: Borel Ruziewicz problem
papers.abstract: We prove that normalized surface measure is the unique finitely additive rotation-invariant probability on the Borel subsets of $S^n$, $n\geq2$. We also prove that Lebesgue measure is the unique finitely additive measure on bounded Borel subsets of $\R^d$, $d\geq3$, invariant under orientation-preserving rigid motions and normalized on the unit cube. The main step is the annihilation of Borel null sets. A spectral gap first gives bounded divergence certificates for compact null sets, chosen in a jointly Borel way. A shared random threshold then combines these certificates to cover arbitrary null sets. For Euclidean space, the construction is applied to families of spheres about two centers; spherical averaging completes the identification of the measure.

papers.title: Classification of fixed points of the centroid body operator
papers.abstract: We classify the fixed points, up to dilation, of the classical volume-normalized centroid body operator in every dimension. We prove that ΓK = cK holds precisely for ellipsoids centered at the origin. The proof combines a signed spherical moment-gap argument in low dimensions with boundary integral operators, compact-group structure, and quantitative regression estimates in higher dimensions. Affine eigenfunctions force a large rotation subspace; curvature and log-concave regression bounds then exclude every proper such subspace. The remaining finite comparisons are certified by exact rational inequalities. The manuscript supplies proofs of the auxiliary analytic estimates and explicitly identifies the external results used.

papers.title: Cross-Energy of Dirichlet Partial Sums. Part 10: The Caceres Prime Function. A square-root damped prime weight, its exact Prime Zeta structure, and a dual spectrum of the Riemann zeros
papers.abstract: \sloppy We study the \emph{Caceres Prime Function} \[ \C(s)=\sum_{n\ge 2}\frac{a(n)}{n^{s}},\qquad a(n)=\sum_{p^k\,\|\,n}\frac{\log p}{\sqrt{p^{k}}}, \] the Dirichlet series of the additive function that weights each prime factor $p$ of $n$ by $\log p$ divided by the square root of the exact power of $p$ dividing $n$. \emph{Structure.} We prove that $\C=\zeta\K$, where the \emph{prime kernel}, $\K(s)=\sum_p\log p\,(1-p^{-s})/(p^{s+1/2}-1)$, is an exact telescoping series of shifted derivatives of the Prime Zeta function. So $\K$ is meromorphic in $\Re s>-\frac14$, and the line $\Re s=-\frac14$ is a natural boundary. Every zero $\frac12+i\gamma$ of $\zeta$ produces two singular points of $\K$, at $i\gamma$ and $i\gamma/2$, which are poles unless $2\gamma$ is again an ordinate with twice the multiplicity (respectively $\gamma/2$ an ordinate with half the multiplicity, for $i\gamma/2$); the exponent $\frac12$ is the normalization that puts both families on the imaginary axis. More precisely, $\K(s)=-\frac{\zeta'}\zeta(s+\frac12)+\frac{\zeta'}\zeta(2s+\frac12)-\frac1{12s}+H(s)$, with $H$ holomorphic in a neighbourhood of $\Re s\ge0$. \emph{RH criteria.} RH is equivalent to the holomorphy of $\K(s)-\frac1{s-1/2}+\frac1{2(s-1/4)}$ in $\Re s>0$. It is also equivalent to a bound $O(x^\varepsilon)$, or even a one-sided bound, for the remainder $R_b$ of the kernel's partial sums. Both are exact reformulations of RH, not proofs. \emph{Mean value and explicit formula.} Unconditionally, $\sum_{n\le x}a(n)=\K(1)x+2\zeta(\frac12)\sqrt x+O(\sqrt x\,e^{-c_\ast\sqrt{\log x}})$, with the explicit bound $5.51\sqrt x$ for the error after the first term when $x\ge10^6$. Under RH, the Riesz mean of $a$ has an explicit formula in which every zero contributes the pure phases $x^{i\gamma}$ and $x^{i\gamma/2}$ at constant amplitude. \emph{The Ces\`aro margin.} The kernel is Suzuki's one-variable margin $M$ seen at two scales. Unconditionally, $R_b(x)=\alpha(x)-\alpha(\sqrt x)+o(1)$, where $\alpha$ is the slope of the margin. Under RH, the kernel's Riesz margin is $M(N)-2M(\sqrt N)$. Its fluctuation has energy $2(\log\xi)''(\frac12)$, reduced by $2\gamma^{-2}$ for every pair of ordinates with $\gamma'=2\gamma$; the near pair $\gamma_{14}\approx2\gamma_4$ is visible in the data. \emph{Zeros of $\C$.} A computer-assisted proof shows that $\C$ has a zero near $1.379+8.639\,i$, in the half-plane of absolute convergence, and Bohr's theory gives $\gg T$ such zeros up to height $T$. So $\C$ is not an $L$-function. The theorems are proved here, except that Section~\ref{sec:margin} uses the formula for the margin and the almost periodicity of the slope from Part~11. Uncertified computations are labelled as numerical observations.

papers.title: Cross-Energy of Dirichlet Partial Sums. Part 16: How many positive directions does the Archimedean place have? A counting law with a boundary phase
papers.abstract: Restrict the archimedean part of Weil's quadratic form, for $\zeta$ or for a primitive real Dirichlet $L$-function of conductor $q$ and parity $\kappa$, to test functions supported in an interval of length $a$, and let $n_+(a)$ be the number of its positive directions, the directions that the pole and the primes must absorb. A Szeg\H{o}-type argument gives $n_+(a)=t_0a/\pi+o(a)$, where $t_0$ is the zero of $\vartheta'$. We observe that the form is $\Lambda-\psi_\kappa(-\Delta)$ with $\psi_\kappa$ a complete Bernstein function (proved) and, using the boundary phase of Kaleta, Kwa\'snicki and Ma{\l}ecki, we state, as a conjecture, the asymptotic law \[ n_+(a)=\Big\lfloor\frac{t_0a}\pi+\frac{2\varpi_\kappa(t_0)}\pi\Big\rfloor , \] with an explicit phase $\varpi_\kappa$ that depends only on the parity, the conductor entering only through $t_0$. We test it in seven cases, $\zeta$ and $\chi_{-3},\chi_{-4},\chi_5,\chi_{-7},\chi_8,\chi_{-8}$. On the finest mesh the shifts of the jumps $m=2,\dots,12$ bracket the prediction $2\varpi_\kappa(t_0)/\pi$, which ranges from $0.18$ to $0.59$, to within $1$ to $3\cdot10^{-3}$ for the characters and $3\cdot10^{-2}$ for $\zeta$. A second, independent implementation extrapolates in the mesh on three to nine jumps per case; the extrapolated shifts lie above the prediction by $0.2$ to $2.3\cdot10^{-4}$ in every case, a one-sided offset of the size of the extrapolation error, which we have checked to be a bias in one case only. The first jump is an exception, and for $\zeta$ the shift reaches its limit only after about ten jumps. A smoothed count removes the integer part and leaves ``degree plus constant'' with the boundary phase as constant; on a circle the constant is carried by the end points and cancels between an arc and its complement; and treating $-\log q$ as a degree, $q\leftrightarrow1/q$ acts on the band edge as $t_0\mapsto4\pi^2/t_0$ to leading order, with $\zeta$ at the self-dual point $t_0\approx2\pi$. We record what the law implies for the signature of Weil's form and where it stands with respect to the Riemann--Roch formulas for $\overline{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z}$. The law is a conjecture supported by these computations. The Bernstein structure is proved here; the first-order count is quoted from Part~14 and its proof is not repeated.

papers.title: Cross-Energy of Dirichlet Partial Sums. Part 37: The $6k\pm1$ race: sieve structure, Chebyshev's bias and a GRH-equivalent inequality
papers.abstract: Every prime $p>3$ is $6k+1$ or $6k-1$. We collect what can be proved about the two resulting sequences and add three results. The races are those modulo $3$ (the prime $2$ counts for the class $2$); the race modulo $6$ differs by that one prime. (i) In the weighting $n^{-1/2}\log(N/n)$ of the Ces\`aro margin, the race between the prime powers $\equiv2$ and $\equiv1\pmod3$ is an exact identity. The $6k-1$ side leads by $2\frac{L'}L(\frac12,\chi_{-3})\log N-\frac12\psi'(\frac34)=1.1320\log N-1.2709$ plus the margin $M_\chi(N)$ of $L(s,\chi_{-3})$. The generalized Riemann hypothesis (GRH) for $L(s,\chi_{-3})$ is equivalent to $M_\chi\ge0$ for all large $N$, and under GRH the weighted race is never lost after $N=2$. This is a criterion of the type of Hardy--Littlewood and Landau (1918) for Chebyshev's assertion, here with the Ces\`aro weight and with explicit constants. (ii) We verify $0.1024\le M_\chi(N)\le0.3549$ for $2\le N\le2^{27}$, inside the window $[0,0.4536]$ that GRH predicts. We also check the formula against the first $271$ zeros of $L(s,\chi_{-3})$. (iii) For the unweighted race, the bias is $1/\sqrt{V_\chi}=2.97$ standard deviations, with $V_\chi=\sum_\rho\frac1{\rho(1-\rho)}=0.113230$ (equal to $\sum_\rho|\rho|^{-2}$ under GRH); under GRH and linear independence, a recomputation with $271$ zeros gives the density $0.99906$, in agreement with the $0.9990$ of Rubinstein and Sarnak. Along the way we prove the sieve characterization of $6k\pm1$ and of twin primes, explain why Legendre-type counting cannot give the error term, compare twin primes and Goldbach representations modulo $6$ with the Hardy--Littlewood predictions, and prove the formula for $\gcd_p(p^{2n}-1)$ (the sequence $24,240,504,480,\dots$). Version~2 adds the generating function $\frac12[\zeta_6(s)^2\pm L(s,\chi_6)^2]$ of the three forms $6xy\pm x\pm y$, and a duality theorem: averaged over the zeros of $\zeta$, the cross-energy $\mathcal C_2(N,\frac12,\gamma)$ of Part~1 returns $\log N/N$; averaged over the zeros of $L(s,\chi_{-3})$ it returns $\frac1N\sum_{d\mid N}\chi_{-3}(d)\Lambda(d)$; and M\"obius inversion separates the primes of the two lanes. Version~3 makes this exact at finite height and without RH: with a Gaussian weight on the zeros, the cross-energy satisfies an explicit formula whose pole term is $\mathcal C_2$ itself at $s=0$, whose prime term is $\log N$ exactly plus a nonnegative remainder from the near coincidences $nj\approx N$, and which returns every prime power up to $60$ from the $1517$ zeros below $2000$. Nothing here proves RH, GRH, or the twin prime or Goldbach conjectures.

papers.title: Exact projector-rank thresholds for state-independent contextuality
papers.abstract: For every integer r ≥ 1 we construct a finite exclusivity graph Fr with the following two properties. First, Fr has a projective representation by pairwise distinct projectors of rank r that exhibits state-independent contextuality. Second, no projective representation of Fr by projectors of any common rank s < r, in any finite dimension, exhibits state-independent contextuality; in every such representation the maximally mixed state is noncontextual. This establishes, for every r, the “rank efficient” scenarios sought by Hohn, Xu and Kleinmann, for which only numerical evidence at r = 2, 3 was available. The graph is the disjunctive product of an odd cycle C2r+1 with the orthogonality structure of a rank-one contextuality set whose fractional chromatic number exceeds its dimension by an arbitrarily small amount. Such sets are obtained from the infinite family of Kochen–Specker parity proofs in R^4 of Elford and Lisonek, together with a coning construction that raises the dimension by one.

papers.title: Explicit bounds for odd perfect and quasiperfect numbers
papers.abstract: Let $N$ be an odd perfect number or a quasiperfect number, and let $B(N) = \prod_{p \mid N} (1+1/p)$. We prove that $2 < N/\varphi(N) < 2.17372$ and that $105 \nmid N$, and we obtain explicit two-sided bounds for $B(N)$ according to the value of $\gcd(15,N)$. For an odd perfect number $N$, they give $B(N) > 1.90281$, $1.70584$, $1.83233$ and $1.67856$ when $\gcd(15,N) = 1$, $3$, $5$ and $15$, respectively, and $B(N) < 1.84348$, $1.93549$ and $1.84125$ when $\gcd(15,N) = 3$, $5$ and $15$. These follow from general bounds for $B(n)$ in terms of $n/\varphi(n)$, of the abundancy index $I(n) = \sigma(n)/n$, and of $\sum_{p \mid n} 1/p$. We also bound the abundancy indices of $N \operatorname{rad}(N)$ and $N/\operatorname{rad}(N)$ and the functions $\sigma^{\pm}$, $\varphi^{+}$ and $\psi^{+}$ of S\'andor and Atanassov at $N$, give an explicit lower bound for the number of distinct prime factors of $N$ in terms of its least prime factor, and show that the sum of the reciprocals of the prime factors of a quasiperfect number $N$ is less than $\log I(N)$. Finally, for the shifted abundancy indices $I^{+}(n) = 1 + \sum_{d \mid n, \, d > 1} 1/(d+1)$ and $I^{-}(n) = 1 + \sum_{d \mid n, \, d > 1} 1/(d-1)$, we determine the optimal constants in the comparisons of $I^{+}$, $I$ and $I^{-}$ on the odd integers and on the odd integers with at most one odd exponent, and we deduce $1.8471 < I^{+}(N) < 2 < I^{-}(N) < 2.2722$ and $I^{-}(N) - I^{+}(N) < 0.42493$ for every odd perfect number $N$.

papers.title: Finite-preparation response under heavy-tailed catastrophes: exact amplitudes and separation from Poisson coverage
papers.abstract: We determine the terminal response of a one-dimensional binary recovery process to a finite preparation history under independently renewed Poisson interval catastrophes. For regularly varying interval weights $\nu_r\sim r^{-p}L(r)$, $p>3$, and fixed small positive intensities, we prove an exact leading response when preparation and observation durations grow proportionally. The main result expresses the response as an explicit functional of the actual recovery-front speeds accumulated along each fixed finite-stage preparation history and of the selected target-phase open density. Its weak-intensity second variation is a strictly positive quadratic form in every nonzero fixed signed temporal modulation, including equal-dose redistributions. A separate four-update theorem identifies local cooperation through an explicit positive equal-dose contrast for every nonzero interval law with finite first moment. These positive contrasts separate the process from conditional Poisson Boolean coverage with fixed grain kernels, a fixed environment distribution and affine intensity control, whose contrast is nonpositive at every finite time. As an effective extension, relative power-law tail bounds yield a conservative computable sufficient threshold valid at every later integer time. The core proof combines nonstationary front transfer, uniform background forgetting and exact resetting at intensity switches.

papers.title: Genuinely multipartite bound entanglement of three qubits
papers.abstract: If a three-party state is positive under partial transposition (PPT) across each of its three bipartitions, no local protocol can distil any pure entanglement from it: neither singlets between any two parties nor GHZ states. All of its entanglement is bound. We show that such a state can nevertheless be genuinely multipartite entangled (GME), meaning that it cannot be prepared by mixing states in each of which some party is unentangled from the rest. This already happens for three qubits, the smallest system in which the question arises and a common experimental setting for multipartite entanglement; to our knowledge no three-qubit example was known. An explicit mixture of five orthogonal states (one GHZ-type, three $W$-type and one product state) is PPT across every cut and GME throughout an exact parameter interval, and its rank, five, is the minimum possible. Genuine entanglement is proved by a witness acting only on the five-dimensional support, whose nonnegativity on the biseparable states in that support reduces to a sum of squares on its curves of product vectors. Such states are invisible to the PPT-mixture test, the standard semidefinite relaxation used to certify GME, yet they form a set with nonempty interior among density matrices: an explicit full-rank example remains GME under $2.33\%$ white noise, while $2.336\%$ makes it biseparable. We also construct extreme examples with the smallest possible partial-transpose ranks $(5,5,5,5)$. All our explicit states, including the full-rank one, lie in the mixed $W$ class: they are mixtures of pure states with vanishing three-tangle, so their genuine entanglement needs no GHZ-type component. Full PPT therefore does not imply biseparability, even for three qubits.

papers.title: Irrational even beta values from powered hypergeometric kernels
papers.abstract: For the Dirichlet beta function, we prove that at least one of $\beta(6),\beta(8),\ldots,\beta(74)$ is irrational, and that at least one of $\beta(8),\beta(10),\ldots,\beta(110)$ is irrational. These shorten the previously stated intervals with the same starting indices, whose upper endpoints are $92$ and $128$, respectively (twinheterodox, Hexagon 2611.00160v2, Section 8.2). The new bounds come from a different construction, based on powers of Krisman's hypergeometric kernel (Hexagon 2610.00285v2).

papers.title: Joint distribution of factorial units and valuations in translated intervals
papers.abstract: For every fixed finite set of primes, the corresponding prime valuations of factorials, reduced modulo arbitrary fixed integers, and the prime-free parts, reduced modulo arbitrary fixed prime powers, have a joint uniform distribution. We give a proof with a power-saving error on every interval of consecutive nonnegative integers, uniform in the interval's starting point. A fixed congruence on the index may be imposed independently. The resulting statement for the part of a factorial coprime to an arbitrary fixed modulus gives the densities and relative density asked for in Problems 2 and 3 of Hajdu and Papp. The proof uses a finite digit-window identity, a strict local character contraction, and a carry estimate followed by finite Fourier analysis.

papers.title: Laurent Phenomenon Algebras on Minuscule Grassmannians and their Mirrors
papers.abstract: We construct Laurent phenomenon algebra structures on the homogeneous coordinate rings of the half-spin Grassmannians and the Freudenthal variety. Their frozen variables are the linear coordinates in a Coxeter orbit, and the resulting boundary divisors are anticanonical. Together with the construction of Daisey--Ducat for the Cayley plane, these examples admit explicit mirrors described by Newton polytopes. We identify the upper Laurent phenomenon algebras of the mirror seeds with the intrinsic mirror algebras of Keel--Yu at the specialization $q^\beta=1$, including the theta functions associated with the individual boundary components. The half-spin construction is uniform in the rank. In the exceptional cases, contact calculations and Laurent divisibility determine the local expansions; the Freudenthal comparison also uses exact calculations of divisorial valuations. We obtain integral comparisons and valuative independence of the intrinsic theta basis in every reachable seed.

papers.title: Marked-point modules and central nilpotents at roots of unity
papers.abstract: We study extensions in the two-marked-point representation of the periodic Temperley--Lieb algebra at $q=e^{i\pi/p}$, $p\in\mathbb Z_{\geq3}$. For every positive even size $N$, we construct a submodule $Z_N$ extending $T_N=W_{N;2,\varepsilon}$ by $W_N=W_{N;0,\varepsilon q}$, where $\varepsilon=\pm1$. The dual trees of noncrossing matchings give an explicit injection $\Theta_N:T_N\to W_N$. Both central braid transfer elements have nilpotent part $g\Theta_N\pi_N$ on $Z_N$, where $\pi_N$ is the quotient map and $g=x+x^{-1}+\varepsilon(y+y^{-1})$ for the marked-point parameters $x,y\in\mathbb{C}^\times$. The extension splits exactly when $g=0$, and the formula determines the central Jordan forms at every even size. In the window $2\leq N<2p-2$, $Z_N$ is a joint central summand and, when $g\ne0$, has simple layers $T_N/S_N/T_N$. An explicit intertwiner and annular localization identify its two-layer quotient with a periodic XXZ sector. The associated basic image algebras have dimensions five and four; the quotient preserves first extensions between simples and kills a nonzero Yoneda product in degree two. An annular operator detects the extension with coefficient $2\varepsilon g$. Beyond the isolated window, we determine a five-simple image algebra and compute a $43$-dimensional joint central summand at $p=3,N=6$, on which the two central nilpotents generate a four-dimensional algebra. Exact matrix calculations and verification code accompany these finite computations.

papers.title: Nonstabilization of the Predictive Boolean Lookahead Hierarchy
papers.abstract: We study the hierarchy of languages generated by predictive Boolean $\mathrm{LL}(k)$ grammars. The model uses a deterministic recursive-descent table, strongly non-left-recursive rules, and at least one positive conjunct per rule. For every integer $r\geq1$, we construct a language over a fixed eight-letter alphabet that has an ordinary $\mathrm{LL}(r+r2^r+2)$ grammar and establish that it has no predictive Boolean $\mathrm{LL}(r)$ grammar. The construction asks for a specified token in a uniquely decodable word. The lower bound represents parsing on a long unary prefix by finitely many forward-moving endpoint streams and a finite Boolean recurrence. Random binary blocks followed by homogeneous blocks separate streams with a persistent timing error from streams having an exact finite-state potential. A bounded-lookahead argument hides a token-count change from each remaining stream. An encoding of the resulting independent queries is then shorter than their arbitrary binary payload. This gives nonstabilization under the stated predictive convention. The conclusion is for the stated parser model, including positive-conjunct and strong non-left-recursion requirements. Path-dependent tables satisfying these requirements give the same language families.

papers.title: On the local geometry of the tight 39-point code in the octonionic projective plane
papers.abstract: Cohn, Kumar and Minton constructed a four-parameter family of tight $39$-point codes in the octonionic projective plane. We show that near each member outside a closed nowhere-dense set of resonant parameters, the labeled tight codes modulo $F_4$ form exactly four ten-dimensional families, any two meeting in the four-parameter family, although the first-order deformations of the member form a $28$-dimensional space modulo $F_4$. The originally constructed code is resonant, and we do not determine the tight codes near it; but every neighborhood of it in the space of unlabeled tight $39$-point codes modulo $F_4$ contains a nonempty open subset homeomorphic to an open subset of $\mathbb R^{10}$, so any neighborhood of it that is a manifold has dimension ten.

papers.title: On the structure of countable hyperspaces of regular subcontinua
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a metric continuum and let $\mathcal D(X)$ be its hyperspace of regular subcontinua, that is, of the subcontinua of $X$ which are the closure of their interior. We prove that if $\mathcal D(X)$ is countable, then the interiors of its minimal elements are dense in $X$, and every regular subcontinuum is determined by the minimal elements it contains. We further establish that $\mathcal D(X)$ is a $G_\delta$ subset of the hyperspace $C(X)$ of subcontinua whenever $X$ admits a family of regular subcontinua whose interiors have dense union and which satisfies an absorption property. Consequently, every countable $\mathcal D(X)$ is completely metrizable and scattered. In particular, $\mathcal D(X)$ is never homeomorphic to the rational numbers, which answers a question of Ramírez Angarita and of Camargo, Ordoñez and Ramírez. The theorems of the paper are formalized in Lean 4.

papers.title: Osterwalder–Schrader axioms for scalar QED$_3$ in the Higgs phase
papers.abstract: We study scalar quantum electrodynamics in three dimensions (QED$_3$) in its Higgs phase: the three-dimensional lattice abelian Higgs model in unitary gauge, with the Villain action, on lattices whose spacing tends to zero with canonically scaled couplings. At each spacing we construct infinite-volume states, as limit points of the periodic states and as limits of states in finite boxes; they carry the lattice symmetries, reflection positivity and bounds uniform in the volume. For the smeared curvature and bounded functions of the density, the generating functionals converge along a subsequence of spacings to a translation-invariant limit functional with the continuity required for the Osterwalder–Schrader reconstruction. For the limits built on the box states, and on the periodic states along dyadic sequences of sides, the limit curvature field satisfies the axioms OS0–OS3, with invariance under the full Euclidean group. The cluster axiom OS4 is proved in a weak form, on almost every ergodic component. The tools are Gaussian domination of the Villain curvature, Ginibre inequalities and reflection positivity.

papers.title: Periodic counterexamples to three conjectures on Kolakoski transforms
papers.abstract: The simple Kolakoski transform need not preserve the limiting mean of a periodic word on $\{1,2\}$. We give a counterexample with input period $24$ and output period $12$, and a balanced counterexample whose input has mean $3/2$ while its output has mean $13/9$. Both examples remain unchanged under every realization of a nonconstant summable perturbation of the weights. Their discrepancies from the input means are linear. Consequently they contradict Conjectures (1), (2), and (4) of Cloitre. These statements concern auxiliary transforms of periodic inputs; the classical Kolakoski frequency problem remains open.

papers.title: Sharp Ionization Bounds for Helium and Lithium
papers.abstract: How many electrons can a nucleus bind? In the non-relativistic Coulomb model, Lieb proved in 1984 that a nucleus of charge $Z$ binds fewer than $2Z+1$ electrons. While this bound has been improved, the sharp upper bound has remained unknown for any nucleus other than hydrogen. We solve this problem for $Z=2$ and $Z=3$ by proving that helium binds two or fewer electrons and lithium binds four or fewer. Both bounds are sharp. Our main tool is an adaptation of Lieb's argument with a quadratic weight, which reduces the nonbinding of doubly negative ions to finitely many inequalities that we verify in a computer-assisted proof.

papers.title: Some positivity properties of Riemann $\Xi$ under smoothing
papers.abstract: We show that smoothing the zeros of the Riemann $\Xi$-function makes it easy to establish positivity properties that are otherwise hard (as they are equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis). Specifically, we smooth each zero with a small density centered at it, and then test the impact of this smoothing on complete monotonicity (CM) of the heat sum $H(t)=\sum_\rho e^{-tz_\rho^2}$ over the zeros $\tfrac12+iz_\rho$. A sufficiently wide density quickly implies CM of the smoothed heat sum. We bound the width (i.e., half-variance) the density needs using increasingly precise facts about the zeros. If we only use that they lie in the critical strip, half-variance $1/8$ suffices; the primes lower this width to $\pi^2/288$; and zeros verified through height $T$ further lower it to $\pi^2/(8\log^2T)$ asymptotically. Ultimately, however, smoothing seems to be of limited utility: despite the CM result, the smoothed reciprocal laws of $\Xi$ are not even log-concave, unlike the unsmoothed ones.

papers.title: The classic enumeration of genera of even definite lattices
papers.abstract: We revisit the enumeration of a genus of even positive definite lattices by Kneser neighbours, certified by the mass. We work at primes dividing the determinant, where the projective spaces are smallest, schedule the exploration of the neighbour graph by a random walk and by orders based on a Hecke bookkeeping, and compute canonical forms through the Weyl chamber of the root system. Genera of rank up to 19 with up to 40,617 classes are enumerated in minutes.

papers.title: The exact diameter of the symmetric group 𝑆𝑛 with LRX generators
papers.abstract: We consider the undirected Cayley graph of the symmetric group 𝑆𝑛 with respect to the cyclic shift 𝐿, its inverse 𝑅, and the transposition 𝑋 of the first two positions. We prove that its diameter is given by 𝑛(𝑛 − 1)/2 for every 𝑛 ≥ 4, thus settling a conjecture open since at least 2011. This is done by separately establishing sharp upper and lower bounds, invoking a variety of combinatorial and group-theoretic arguments which leave a finite set of special cases that are verified in the accompanying C++ code. We also provide a Lean formalization of the results.

papers.title: The Quantum Kazhdan–Lusztig Conjecture for Quantum Loop Algebras
papers.abstract: We prove the quantum Kazhdan–Lusztig conjecture for finite-dimensional type 1 representations of untwisted quantum loop algebras at every non-root-of-unity complex parameter.

papers.title: Unitary character moments and a zero-free half-plane for unitary Weil L-functions
papers.abstract: We extend Liu's moment estimate for ordinary ideal-character sums to two independent fixed unitary twists, preserving the full length range of the finite-order theorem. The proof keeps the two character coefficients separate through the Gauss transformations and controls exceptional terms by the poles of their Mellin transforms. The case of two equal twists strengthens the fourth moment used in zero detection. Using the analytic results of Hu and Liu specified in the paper, we obtain the zero-free half-plane $\operatorname{Re}s>(777-\sqrt{1081})/852=0.8733819666\ldots$ for every unitary Hecke $L$-function over every number field, including characters of infinite order. This extends the known finite-order bound to the full unitary family. Unitary induction gives the same half-plane for finite-dimensional continuous unitary Weil representations, with the norm-character poles counted exactly.
